verses.text: But on the first day of the week, at early dawn, they and some others came to the tomb, bringing the spices which they had prepared.
They found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
They entered in, and didn’t find the Lord Jesus’ body.
While they were greatly perplexed about this, behold, two men stood by them in dazzling clothing.

Becoming terrified, they bowed their faces down to the earth.
They said to them, “Why do you seek the living among the dead?
He isn’t here, but is risen. Remember what he told you when he was still in Galilee,
saying that the Son of Man must be delivered up into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again?”
They remembered his words,
returned from the tomb, and told all these things to the eleven, and to all the rest.
Now they were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Mary the mother of James. The other women with them told these things to the apostles.
These words seemed to them to be nonsense, and they didn’t believe them.
But Peter got up and ran to the tomb. Stooping and looking in, he saw the strips of linen lying by themselves, and he departed to his home, wondering what had happened.
Behold, two of them were going that very day to a village named Emmaus, which was sixty stadia from Jerusalem.
They talked with each other about all of these things which had happened.
While they talked and questioned together, Jesus himself came near, and went with them.
But their eyes were kept from recognizing him.

He said to them,
“What are you talking about as you walk, and are sad?”
One of them, named Cleopas, answered him, “Are you the only stranger in Jerusalem who doesn’t know the things which have happened there in these days?”
and how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him up to be condemned to death, and crucified him.
But we were hoping that it was he who would redeem Israel. Yes, and besides all this, it is now the third day since these things happened.
Also, certain women of our company amazed us, having arrived early at the tomb;
and when they didn’t find his body, they came saying that they had also seen a vision of angels, who said that he was alive.
Some of us went to the tomb, and found it just like the women had said, but they didn’t see him.”

He said to them,
“Foolish men, and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!
Didn’t the Christ have to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?”
Beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he explained to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.
They came near to the village, where they were going, and he acted like he would go further.

They urged him, saying, “Stay with us, for it is almost evening, and the day is almost over.”
He went in to stay with them.
When he had sat down at the table with them, he took the bread and gave thanks. Breaking it, he gave it to them.
Their eyes were opened, and they recognized him, and he vanished out of their sight.
They said to one another, “Weren’t our hearts burning within us, while he spoke to us along the way, and while he opened the Scriptures to us?”
They rose up that very hour, returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and those who were with them,
saying, “The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon!”
They related the things that happened along the way, and how he was recognized by them in the breaking of the bread.

As they said these things, Jesus himself stood among them, and said to them,
“Peace be to you.”
But they were terrified and filled with fear, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.

He said to them,
“Why are you troubled? Why do doubts arise in your hearts?
See my hands and my feet, that it is truly me. Touch me and see, for a spirit doesn’t have flesh and bones, as you see that I have.”
When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.

While they still didn’t believe for joy, and wondered, he said to them,
“Do you have anything here to eat?”
They gave him a piece of a broiled fish and some honeycomb.
He took them, and ate in front of them.

He said to them,
“This is what I told you, while I was still with you, that all things which are written in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms, concerning me must be fulfilled.”
Then he opened their minds, that they might understand the Scriptures.

He said to them,
“Thus it is written, and thus it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead the third day,
and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name to all the nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
You are witnesses of these things.
Behold, I send out the promise of my Father on you. But wait in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high.”
He led them out as far as Bethany, and he lifted up his hands, and blessed them.
While he blessed them, he withdrew from them, and was carried up into heaven.
They worshiped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
and were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.

items.label: M1
items.outcome: arrival at the tomb with spices
items.paraphrase: The women plus some others arrive at the tomb at daybreak carrying the prepared spices.
items.gloss: They come as mourners doing what love requires — the burial rites the sabbath had interrupted; the reader meets them not as witnesses to a miracle but as women faithful to a corpse.
items.sitz: post-burial visit to a tomb to tend a corpse
items.paradigm: Jewish burial customs; women's mourning role

items.label: M2
items.paraphrase: They discover the stone has been rolled back from the tomb's entrance.
items.gloss: The sealed threshold is already unsealed before they arrive; something has acted here before them, and the ordinary work of tending the dead is quietly overtaken.

items.label: M3
items.paraphrase: They go inside the tomb.
items.gloss: They cross the threshold anyway — grief keeps its appointment even when the setting has changed under their feet.

items.label: M4
items.paraphrase: Inside, they do not find the Lord Jesus' body.
items.gloss: The absence is registered before it is interpreted; what love came to do cannot be done, and the reader feels the hollow before anyone names it.

items.label: M5
items.paraphrase: They become deeply puzzled by the absence.
items.gloss: The women are not yet given a meaning for what they see — the account lingers honestly in the blank space where an answer should be.

items.label: M6
items.paraphrase: Suddenly two men in shining garments are standing beside them.
items.gloss: Into the blank space something breaks in from outside — the source of understanding is no longer the women's own looking but a word arriving from beyond them.

lineage.seam: Is the pair of men in dazzling clothing standing on the Danielic angelophany type-scene, and if so does the revelatory-interpreter role of t

items.label: M7
items.substrate: the appearance of the two men
items.paraphrase: The women become terrified.
items.gloss: The right response to a heavenly presence is not curiosity but dread; the fear itself is a form of accurate recognition.

items.label: M8
items.substrate: their own faces / to the earth
items.paraphrase: They bow their faces down to the ground.
items.gloss: The body knows what the mind has not yet caught up to — bowing enacts the acknowledgment that something greater than them is standing there.

items.label: M9
items.paraphrase: The two men address the women with a question.
items.gloss: The heavenly figures do not merely announce; they engage — the women are addressed as ones capable of being spoken to and answering back.
items.sitz: angelic address at the empty tomb

items.label: M10
items.paraphrase: They challenge the women for looking for a living one where the dead lie.
items.gloss: The question is really a correction: they are looking in the wrong category, and their expectation itself is what needs to be reset.
items.sitz: angelic interpretation of the empty tomb

items.label: M11
items.paraphrase: They declare that he is not present here but has been raised.
items.gloss: The absence is finally given its meaning from above — what looked like loss is announced as something wholly new that has been done to him.

items.label: M12
items.substrate: the women's memory / his prior words
items.paraphrase: They tell the women to recall what he said back in Galilee.
items.gloss: The new event is anchored to a word already spoken — they are not asked to believe on the spot but to bring an earlier teaching back to mind.
items.sitz: angelic prompt to recollect prior teaching

items.label: M13
items.narrator: the two men, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: Jesus, back in Galilee, told them beforehand what would happen to the Son of Man.
items.gloss: The teaching being invoked belongs to him — his own prior words become the frame through which today's emptiness is to be read.

items.label: M14
items.agent: not-stated (divine passive) — the Son of Man as patient
items.outcome: handed over, crucified, and raised on the third day
items.narrator: the two men quoting Jesus, via the narrator
items.paraphrase: The content foretold: the Son of Man must be handed over to sinful men, be crucified, and on the third day rise again.
items.gloss: The pattern he laid down — handed over, killed, raised — is presented not as accident but as something that had to unfold this way.
items.sitz: prophetic necessity in Jesus' Galilean teaching

Is the divine-passive 'must be handed over to sinful men' standing on the Servant who was 'handed over' for the iniquity of others, and if s
imports the Danielic 'Son of Man' title as the subject of a passion-and-resurrection prediction, but leaves unsaid whether the exalted heave

items.label: M15
items.paraphrase: The women call his earlier words to mind.
items.gloss: The recognition happens inwardly first: the past teaching clicks into place and reframes the present without anyone having to argue it to them.

items.label: M16
items.paraphrase: The women head back from the tomb.
items.gloss: Understanding turns immediately into motion — a private insight becomes an errand back to the community.

items.label: M17
items.substrate: the eleven and all the rest
items.outcome: the events reported to the group
items.paraphrase: They report everything that happened to the eleven and to the rest of the followers.
items.gloss: The women are the first to carry the news; the account places the announcement of the resurrection in their mouths before anyone else's.
items.sitz: first witness-report of the empty tomb

items.label: M18
items.paraphrase: The narrator identifies the women as Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary mother of James, and other women with them.
items.gloss: The narrator pauses to name them — not anonymous mourners but particular, identifiable people whose word can be checked.

items.label: M19
items.outcome: the events reported to the apostles
items.paraphrase: The other women with them likewise report these things to the apostles.
items.gloss: The report is not one voice but many — the message is corroborated within the women's own circle before it ever reaches the men.

items.label: M20
items.paraphrase: The words strike the hearers as idle nonsense.
items.gloss: The hearers hear the words as empty chatter; the message is present but the room is closed against it.

items.label: M21
items.paraphrase: They refuse to believe the women.
items.gloss: The refusal deepens from dismissal into flat unbelief — the women are trusted messengers to a community that will not receive them.

items.label: M22
items.paraphrase: Peter, however, gets up and runs off to the tomb.
items.gloss: One hearer at least is unsettled enough to check — disbelief in the room does not fully cover a private need to see.

items.label: M23
items.substrate: the strips of linen (in the tomb)
items.outcome: observation of the linens lying alone
items.paraphrase: Bending down to look inside, he sees the linen wrappings lying by themselves.
items.gloss: He looks with his own eyes and sees only the leftover cloths — the physical evidence is real but partial, less than an appearance.

items.label: M24
items.paraphrase: He leaves and heads home.
items.gloss: He leaves with less than he came for — the evidence did not resolve into a meaning, and the tomb sends him home unfinished.

items.label: M25
items.paraphrase: He puzzles over what has taken place.
items.gloss: The wondering is left uncompleted on purpose — the account refuses to hand Peter the recognition that will belong to others.

items.label: M26
items.substrate: the village Emmaus (destination; sixty stadia from Jerusalem)
items.paraphrase: That same day, two of the group are traveling to a village called Emmaus, about sixty stadia from Jerusalem.
items.gloss: The next scene starts elsewhere and moves outward — Jerusalem's unresolved report becomes the freight two travelers carry down the road.

items.label: M27
items.substrate: all these things that had happened
items.paraphrase: They discuss with each other everything that has just happened.
items.gloss: Two people trying to sort out what happened by talking it through — the ordinary human work of trying to make grief make sense.

items.label: M28
items.paraphrase: As they talk and question each other, Jesus himself draws near.
items.gloss: The one they are talking about steps into their conversation — the shift is quiet, but the source of what they can now know is no longer only their own memories.

items.label: M29
items.paraphrase: He walks along with them.
items.gloss: He joins their walking rather than announcing himself — a companion on the road before he is anything else.

items.label: M30
items.agent: not-stated (divine passive) — their eyes as patient
items.substrate: the two travelers' recognition of Jesus
items.paraphrase: Their eyes are held so that they cannot recognize him.
items.gloss: The disclosure is deliberately held back — recognition is not something they can seize but something that has to be given at the right moment.
items.sitz: concealed identity of the risen Jesus

items.label: M31
items.paraphrase: Jesus asks the two travelers what they are discussing as they walk along looking sad.
items.gloss: He begins as any stranger might — with a question that opens a conversation rather than an announcement that closes one.
items.sitz: encounter on the road to Emmaus

items.label: M32
items.substrate: the two travelers' conversation and their sadness
items.paraphrase: He asks them what topic they are exchanging with each other while walking, noting their sadness.
items.gloss: The question notices what the walk itself was showing — that they were carrying something heavy in their bodies as they went.

items.label: M33
items.paraphrase: One of them, Cleopas by name, replies to him.
items.gloss: One of them steps forward by name, giving the exchange a particular voice the reader can hold onto.

items.label: M34
items.substrate: Jesus' apparent ignorance of recent Jerusalem events
items.paraphrase: Cleopas asks — with surprise — whether Jesus is the only visitor in Jerusalem who has not learned what has been happening lately there.
items.gloss: The events feel so public to Cleopas that only a stranger could have missed them — the irony is that the one asking IS the events.
items.sitz: road encounter; assumption that the events are common knowledge
items.paradigm: public notoriety of the passion events

items.label: M35
items.paraphrase: Jesus asks them back which things they mean.
items.gloss: He declines to fill in the answer for them — the story has to come out of their own mouths before he can give it back to them differently.

items.label: M36
items.paraphrase: He asks which things they are referring to.
items.gloss: He gives them the room to say it in their own words, letting their account of the events take shape without prompting.

items.label: M37
items.paraphrase: They reply to him.
items.gloss: They take up the invitation to speak — the road becomes the place where their version of the story gets told aloud.

items.label: M38
items.outcome: topic named as Jesus the Nazarene
items.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: They point to the matters concerning Jesus of Nazareth.
items.gloss: They give the story its subject: everything now circles around one person and what happened to him.

items.label: M39
items.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: They characterize Jesus as a prophet powerful in deed and word before God and all the people.
items.gloss: Their summary is admiring but past-tense — he was a great prophet, and that framing is exactly what the following days broke.
items.sitz: public reputation of Jesus prior to the passion

items.label: M40
items.agent: the chief priests and our rulers
items.outcome: handed over to be condemned to death
items.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: They report that the chief priests and their own rulers handed Jesus over for a death sentence.
items.gloss: They name the machinery of his death plainly — their own leadership handed him over; the wound is inside the house.

items.label: M41
items.agent: the chief priests and our rulers
items.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: They report that those same authorities crucified him.
items.gloss: The mode of death is not softened — the specific horror of crucifixion is what is being carried in their grief.

items.label: M42
items.substrate: Jesus as the awaited redeemer of Israel
items.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: They confess they had been hoping he was the one to redeem Israel.
items.gloss: The rawest line: they had staked a hope on him, and speak now from the far side of that hope collapsing.

items.label: M43
items.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: They note that on top of everything else, this is now the third day since these events took place.
items.gloss: Reciting the day-count is a way of measuring how long the silence has held — three days without the reversal they had been taught to expect.
items.sitz: reckoning of days since the crucifixion

items.label: M44
items.agent: certain women of our company (having arrived early at the tomb)
items.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: They add that some women of their group astonished them, having gone to the tomb at early morning.
items.gloss: The women's report enters their own account as one more unsettling piece — received, but not yet trusted enough to change anything.
items.sitz: reception of the women's tomb-report inside the travelers' circle
items.paradigm: astonishing witness of the empty tomb

items.label: M45
items.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: The women did not find his body at the tomb.
items.gloss: The absent body is passed along as the women's finding — a fact the travelers can repeat but not interpret.
items.sitz: the women's tomb-report as retold on the road

items.label: M46
items.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: The women returned and reported what they had seen.
items.gloss: The chain of witness gets one more link: they are quoting women who were quoting what they had seen.
items.sitz: women's testimony recounted on the road

items.label: M47
items.narrator: the women (twice-nested: via the travelers via the narrator)
items.paraphrase: They claimed to have seen a vision of angels.
items.gloss: The angelic sighting is repeated as claim rather than owned as certainty — the travelers place it at arm's length as "what the women said."

items.label: M48
items.narrator: the angels (thrice-nested via women via travelers via narrator)
items.paraphrase: The angels said he was alive.
items.gloss: The core announcement is repeated in the travelers' summary — the message survives the retelling even where belief does not.

items.label: M49
items.paraphrase: He is alive.
items.gloss: The claim in its barest form — three words that the whole account is trying to teach them how to receive.

items.label: M50
items.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: Some of their own group then went to the tomb themselves.
items.gloss: Other members of the group followed up — the report was taken seriously enough to be checked, even if not yet believed.

items.label: M51
items.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: They found conditions matching the women's description.
items.gloss: The tomb's physical state matched the women's account — the men's investigation confirmed the women were not making it up.

items.label: M52
items.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: But they did not see Jesus himself.
items.gloss: Corroboration reached the tomb but not the person — the men could verify the emptiness but not the one who had left it empty.

items.label: M53
items.paraphrase: Jesus responds to them.
items.gloss: He picks up the conversation from inside their account — no announcement, just a response that takes their words seriously enough to answer.
items.sitz: road encounter — Jesus' rebuke and instruction

items.label: M54
items.outcome: the travelers named foolish and slow-hearted
items.paraphrase: He calls them dull-minded and slow at heart to trust everything the prophets said.
items.gloss: The problem, he tells them, was never lack of evidence — it was a heart too slow to trust the scriptures they already knew.

items.label: M55
items.substrate: the necessity of the Christ's suffering-then-glory pattern
items.paraphrase: He asks rhetorically whether the Christ was not obliged to suffer these things and then enter his glory.
items.gloss: The suffering they had experienced as the collapse of the hope was, all along, the shape the hope was supposed to take.

lineage.seam: imports the Servant's necessary suffering as warrant for the Christ's suffering-then-glory pattern, but leaves unsaid whether Isaiah's Serva

items.label: M56
items.substrate: all the scriptures (from Moses and the prophets onward) concerning himself
items.paraphrase: Starting with Moses and running through all the prophets, he interprets to them all the scriptural passages that speak of himself.
items.gloss: He walks them through their own scriptures with him as the key — the texts they knew are reopened around a center they had not seen.

lineage.source_ref: Moses and all the Prophets (Torah + Nevi'im, unspecified loci)
lineage.seam: imports the whole of Moses-and-the-Prophets as a christologically-referring corpus, but leaves unsaid WHICH passages and by what hermeneutic

items.label: M57
items.paraphrase: They approach the village they are heading for.
items.gloss: The teaching has ended and the village is here — the road-conversation reaches its natural stopping point.

items.label: M58
items.paraphrase: He gives the appearance of intending to travel farther.
items.gloss: He does not force his company — the decisive moment is placed inside their freedom to invite him or let him pass.

items.label: M59
items.paraphrase: They press him to stay.
items.gloss: Their pressing is the small opening the whole scene has been waiting for — hospitality is what lets the recognition happen.

items.label: M60
items.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: They ask him to remain with them because it is nearly evening and the day is almost gone.
items.gloss: The reason they give is ordinary — it's getting dark — and the ordinariness is the point: the extraordinary enters through everyday care for a stranger.

items.label: M61
items.paraphrase: He enters to remain with them.
items.gloss: The invitation is accepted; the guest who might have gone past becomes a guest inside a house.

items.label: M62
items.substrate: the table with the two travelers
items.paraphrase: He reclines at table with them.
items.gloss: The stranger they invited in takes his place at their table — the shared meal opens the space where recognition can happen.
items.sitz: evening meal at the Emmaus village

items.label: M63
items.paraphrase: He takes the loaf into his hands.
items.gloss: The guest quietly assumes the host's role — his hands take the bread, and the arrangement of the meal shifts.

lineage.seam: imports the standard Jewish take–bless–break–give host sequence as the vehicle of recognition, but leaves unsaid whether the ordinary domest

items.label: M64
items.substrate: the bread (implicit; blessing said over it)
items.paraphrase: He gives thanks over it.
items.gloss: The blessing is Jewish and ordinary — the recognition to come will hinge on a gesture any Jewish table would recognize.

items.label: M65
items.paraphrase: He breaks the bread.
items.gloss: The bread is broken in the same fourfold sequence they had seen him do before — the shape of the action is what carries the memory.

items.label: M66
items.outcome: bread handed to the two travelers
items.paraphrase: He hands it to them.
items.gloss: The bread passes from his hands to theirs — the sequence completes in the giving, which is where the moment turns.

items.label: M67
items.agent: not-stated (divine passive) — their eyes as patient
items.paraphrase: Their eyes are opened.
items.gloss: What had been held closed is now opened for them; the seeing is granted, not achieved.

lineage.seam: Is the divine-passive 'their eyes were opened' at a shared meal standing on Eden's 'the eyes of both were opened' after eating, and if so do

items.label: M68
items.paraphrase: They recognize him.
items.gloss: The face across the table is suddenly known — the person they had walked and eaten with resolves into who he actually is.

items.label: M69
items.outcome: Jesus no longer visible to them
items.paraphrase: He becomes invisible to them.
items.gloss: In the same instant, he is no longer there — the recognition is complete, and his visible presence is withdrawn precisely at that fullness.

items.label: M70
items.paraphrase: They speak to each other.
items.gloss: The reflex is immediate speech — they need to say to each other what has just happened.

items.label: M71
items.substrate: the traveling encounter and scriptural opening
items.outcome: realization that they had been inwardly kindled
items.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: They ask each other, in retrospect, whether their hearts were not on fire inside them while he was speaking on the road and opening the scriptures.
items.gloss: Looking back, they realize the recognition had already been happening in their bodies while he spoke — the heart knew before the eyes did.
items.sitz: retrospective recognition of the on-road experience

items.label: M72
items.outcome: on their feet, ready to move
items.paraphrase: They stand up at that very hour.
items.gloss: Recognition instantly becomes urgency — the meal is left, the evening ignored; the news cannot wait until morning.

items.label: M73
items.paraphrase: They travel back to Jerusalem.
items.gloss: The retreat from Jerusalem reverses — the same road that carried them away in grief now carries them back with something to say.

items.label: M74
items.substrate: the eleven and those with them
items.paraphrase: They find the eleven together with those in their company.
items.gloss: They arrive to find the community assembled and waiting — the isolated experience is about to enter a shared one.

items.label: M75
items.agent: the eleven and those with them
items.paraphrase: The gathered group is already declaring the news to them.
items.gloss: Before they can speak, they are being spoken to — the news is already breaking out from more than one source at once.

items.label: M76
items.agent: the eleven and those with them
items.outcome: assertion that he is truly risen
items.narrator: the eleven and company, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: They declare that the Lord has truly been raised.
items.gloss: The proclamation now comes out of the community's shared mouth — no longer one witness's claim but the group's confession.

items.label: M77
items.agent: the eleven and those with them
items.narrator: the eleven and company, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: They report that he has appeared to Simon.
items.gloss: A particular appearance to a named leader is attached to the general claim — the news is being anchored in specific people it happened to.

items.label: M78
items.paraphrase: The two travelers narrate what happened on the road.
items.gloss: The Emmaus travelers now add their own strand — first-person testimony joining the pile of others' reports.

items.label: M79
items.substrate: the recognition-event at the breaking of the bread
items.outcome: account of how Jesus was recognized delivered
items.narrator: the travelers, quoted by the narrator
items.paraphrase: They report how he was made known to them in the breaking of the bread.
items.gloss: They give the recognition its distinctive shape — it happened at the breaking of the bread, and that specificity is what they hand to the community.

items.label: M80
items.outcome: Jesus present in the middle of them
items.paraphrase: While they are still telling this, Jesus himself is standing in their midst.
items.gloss: The testimony has barely landed when the one testified to is himself in the room — the reports are overtaken by the person they were about.

items.label: M81
items.paraphrase: He addresses them.
items.gloss: He speaks first — the room does not have to figure out what to do; the initiative comes from him.
items.sitz: first words of the risen Jesus to the group

lineage.seam: Is the 'Peace to you' greeting standing on the Tanakh's shalom-formula (often spoken to reassure a terrified recipient of a theophany), and

items.label: M82
items.paraphrase: He bestows peace on them.
items.gloss: The first word he gives is peace — not proof, not rebuke, but the gift of steadiness offered before anything else.

items.label: M83
items.paraphrase: The group is thrown into terror and fear.
items.gloss: The peace does not land — the actual response to a real appearance is not calm but panic.

items.label: M84
items.outcome: belief that they are seeing a spirit
items.paraphrase: They suppose that what they are seeing is a ghost.
items.gloss: They reach for the category they have — a ghost — because a visible dead person fits nothing else they know.
items.sitz: first-century ghost/spirit construal of an apparition

items.label: M85
items.narrator: the group (as their supposition), reported by the narrator
items.paraphrase: What they are seeing is a spirit.
items.gloss: The supposition names itself: whatever this is, it belongs to the world of shades, not to the world of bodies.

items.label: M86
items.paraphrase: He addresses them.
items.gloss: He answers the misperception by speaking to it directly — the ghost-hypothesis is not left to fade but is met head-on.

items.label: M87
items.paraphrase: He asks why they are agitated.
items.gloss: The question puts their fear back to them as a problem to be examined rather than a mood to be indulged.
items.sitz: reassurance in the middle of terror

items.label: M88
items.substrate: the doubts arising in their hearts
items.outcome: challenge posed to their inner doubting
items.paraphrase: He asks why doubts are welling up in their hearts.
items.gloss: The doubt is treated as a real thing rising inside them — he names the inner motion instead of pretending it isn't there.

items.label: M89
items.substrate: the group's sight of his hands and feet
items.paraphrase: He commands them to look at his hands and his feet to confirm his identity.
items.gloss: He offers his wounded hands and feet as the proof — the marks of the crucifixion are exactly what shows this is the same person.

items.label: M90
items.paraphrase: He commands them to touch him and see for themselves.
items.gloss: Looking is not enough; he invites their hands as well — the proof he offers is willing to be pressed and tested.

items.label: M91
items.paraphrase: He argues that a spirit does not have flesh and bones such as they can see he has.
items.gloss: He rules out the ghost category on its own terms — whatever a spirit is, it isn't this thing you can see and touch.

items.label: M92
items.paraphrase: Having said this, he shows them his hands and feet.
items.gloss: Words are backed with the thing itself — his hands and feet are shown so the argument doesn't have to be trusted, only seen.

items.label: M93
items.outcome: state of joyous disbelief and wonder
items.paraphrase: They still cannot believe it, out of joy, and remain amazed.
items.gloss: The failure to believe here is not resistance but overflow — the good news is too much to take in all at once.

items.label: M94
items.paraphrase: He addresses them again.
items.gloss: Speech restarts the interaction — even the joy that is stopping them has to be moved through, not around.

items.label: M95
items.paraphrase: He asks whether they have any food on hand.
items.gloss: He asks for food as a person would — the request itself is meant to close the last gap between what they are seeing and what they can believe.

items.label: M96
items.substrate: a piece of broiled fish and some honeycomb
items.paraphrase: They hand him a piece of grilled fish and some honeycomb.
items.gloss: They respond with what they have on hand — the exchange becomes as ordinary as a shared supper.

items.label: M97
items.paraphrase: He takes the food from them.
items.gloss: His hand receives what theirs offers — the giving-and-taking is itself a proof no argument could match.

items.label: M98
items.paraphrase: He eats it in their sight.
items.gloss: He eats in front of them — the plainest possible demonstration that the body they are looking at can do what bodies do.

items.label: M99
items.paraphrase: He speaks to them once more.
items.gloss: With the ghost-question settled, the exchange turns to teaching — now that they can believe he is here, he can begin to say what it means.

items.label: M100
items.substrate: his prior teaching about scriptural-fulfillment concerning himself
items.outcome: reminder that all Law-Prophets-Psalms passages about him must be fulfilled
items.paraphrase: He reminds them that while still with them he had told them everything written about him in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms must come to fulfillment.
items.gloss: He anchors the present moment to earlier words — everything happening now had already been laid out in what they knew.

lineage.source_ref: Law of Moses + Prophets + Psalms (tripartite Tanakh)
lineage.seam: imports the tripartite Tanakh (Torah / Nevi'im / Ketuvim-headed-by-Psalms) as a single corpus that must be fulfilled in him, but leaves unsa

items.label: M101
items.outcome: minds opened to understand the scriptures
items.paraphrase: He opens up their minds so they can grasp the scriptures.
items.gloss: Understanding here is given, not achieved — he does something to their minds so the scriptures can finally be read.

items.label: M102
items.paraphrase: He addresses them.
items.gloss: With their understanding opened, he begins to say what it now lets them hear — the illumination is followed by the teaching it was for.

items.label: M103
items.paraphrase: He points to what stands written.
items.gloss: He points them to the written word as the settled ground — what happened had to happen because it stands there in writing.

items.label: M104
items.agent: not-stated (divine passive) — the Christ as patient
items.outcome: suffered and raised on the third day
items.paraphrase: It was necessary that the Christ suffer and rise from the dead on the third day.
items.gloss: The suffering and the rising are laid down together as one required pattern — the cross is not the exception to the plan but the shape of it.

lineage.seam: imports the Servant's necessary suffering and Hosea's third-day rising as scriptural warrant for the Christ's death-and-resurrection pattern

items.label: M105
items.agent: not-stated (divine passive) — content to be proclaimed
items.substrate: repentance and forgiveness of sins in his name
items.outcome: proclamation to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem
items.move_type: proclamation (missional mandate embedded in the necessity)
items.paraphrase: Repentance and forgiveness of sins are to be proclaimed in his name to every nation, starting from Jerusalem.
items.gloss: What has happened to him is meant to travel — the private events of one Jewish week become an announcement aimed at every people.

lineage.seam: imports the Isaianic vision of a message going out from Zion to the nations as warrant for a Jerusalem-originating proclamation of repentanc

items.label: M106
items.paraphrase: He designates them as witnesses of these things.
items.gloss: Their status shifts from bystanders to witnesses — being present at these things becomes a role they now have to carry.

items.label: M107
items.outcome: the Father's promise sent upon them
items.paraphrase: He announces that he is sending upon them what his Father promised.
items.gloss: The commission comes with a promised gift — they are not being sent on their own strength, and the sending waits on what will be given.
items.sitz: promise of what the Father has pledged

items.label: M108
items.substrate: the group's remaining in Jerusalem until they are clothed with power from on high
items.paraphrase: He commands them to remain in the city until they are clothed with power from on high.
items.gloss: Until the promise arrives, the right posture is stillness — the mission begins with waiting rather than doing.
items.sitz: instruction to stay in Jerusalem until endowed with power

lineage.seam: imports Joel's promise of the Spirit poured out on all flesh as the 'Father's promise' / 'power from on high,' but leaves unsaid whether Joe

items.label: M109
items.substrate: the group (led as far as Bethany)
items.outcome: the group brought out to the vicinity of Bethany
items.paraphrase: He leads them out as far as Bethany.
items.gloss: He takes them out to the edge of the city — the setting of the parting is chosen, not incidental.
items.sitz: leaving Jerusalem for the ascension site

items.label: M110
items.paraphrase: He raises his hands.
items.gloss: Hands raised over a gathered people is the priest's posture — what he is about to do is meant to be seen as blessing, in the old temple sense.

lineage.seam: Is the lifting of the hands to bless standing on the Aaronic priestly gesture of Leviticus 9, and if so does an Aaronic priestly benediction

items.label: M111
items.paraphrase: He blesses them.
items.gloss: The last thing he does to them is bless them — the goodbye is shaped as a gift rather than a farewell.

items.label: M112
items.paraphrase: As the blessing goes on, he departs from them.
items.gloss: The blessing is not interrupted by the leaving — the parting happens inside the giving, so what he was doing to them is what remains.

items.label: M113
items.paraphrase: He is taken up into heaven.
items.gloss: He goes up, and the direction is theological as much as physical — the one who was handed down and killed is now lifted up into God's own place.

lineage.seam: Is the divine-passive being-carried-up-into-heaven standing on Elijah's ascent, and if so does an Elijah-type translation get repurposed as

items.label: M114
items.paraphrase: They worship him.
items.gloss: They give him what only God is given — the response to the ascension names what they now understand him to be.

items.label: M115
items.outcome: return to Jerusalem accomplished, with great joy
items.paraphrase: They return to Jerusalem with great joy.
items.gloss: They walk back the way they came, and the mood of the return is the opposite of what left Jerusalem earlier — joy where there had been grief.

items.label: M116
items.paraphrase: They stay continually present in the temple.
items.gloss: The joy settles into a place — the temple becomes their habitual home, and the resurrection community begins in the old house of prayer.
items.sitz: post-ascension habitual gathering at the Jerusalem temple

items.label: M117
items.paraphrase: They keep praising God.
items.gloss: Praise becomes their steady work — the response to what has happened is not a single act but a continuing life.

items.label: M118
items.paraphrase: They keep blessing God.
items.gloss: Alongside praise, blessing — the Jewish grammar of thanks to God stays the native language of this new community.

items.label: M119
items.paraphrase: An affirming closing word seals the account.
items.gloss: The account signs itself off with a settled Amen — the reader is left inside the affirmation, not on the outside looking at a claim.

reception.title: The resurrection end-silence — how it was received

readers.label: Lake
readers.reading: Lake treats the women's silence as the deliberate, emphatic main point of Mark's ending, while allowing that a now-lost continuation likely explained how they eventually spoke.
readers.quoted_span: the deliberate silence of the women at the beginning — which is the main point — is perfectly plain, for the statement is quite emphatic

readers.label: Orr (1908)
readers.reading: Orr acknowledges Mark breaks off at the women's flight in trembling, but insists Mark's Gospel nonetheless implied — no less than the others — that a report followed.
readers.quoted_span: St. Mark breaks off with the women fleeing from the tomb in "trembling and astonishment" ; but there can be no reasonable doubt that his Gospel also, not less than the others, contemplated a report of t

readers.label: Mark · ICC
readers.reading: Gould normalizes the abrupt ending as consistent with Mark's habitual brevity at the gospel's margins — not strange, not requiring explanation, simply characteristic.
readers.quoted_span: Mark gives merely the announcement of the resurrection to the women by the angels, and closes with this. This, instead of being strange, and requiring explanation, is quite in accordance with the character of Mark

readers.label: Matthew · ICC
readers.reading: Allen reads Mark's silence as naturally inviting a follow-up appearance; Matthew, uneasy with it, rewrites the women as speaking, then continues with the appearance — but unmotivated.
readers.quoted_span: It is very natural that this should have been followed by an appearance to them of Christ dispelling their fear and repeating the angel's message. Mt. alters "and told no one," etc., into "ran to tell His disciples."

readers.label: Longer Ending (16:9–20)
readers.reading: The most consequential reception act: a later hand SUPPLIED an ending — appearances + commission + ascension — precisely because Mark's abrupt 16:8 silence was felt as a gap that had to be closed.

readers.label: Shorter Ending
readers.reading: A second, briefer supplied ending in some manuscripts — independent evidence that the 16:8 silence generated MULTIPLE closure-attempts, not one.

readers.label: Narrative criticism
readers.reading: Reads 16:8 not as a defect or accident but as an INTENTIONAL narrative choice — the silence forces the reader to supply the continuation (the 'hermeneutic of secrecy'). NOT in our corpus (the narrative-critical register is a known coverage gap, IRR228) — added as attested/inferred.

center.label: Mark 16:8 — the end-silence
center.reading: Each account ends on a silence; Mark breaks off abruptly with the women afraid and saying nothing. What happens after is unnarrated, later supplied, or left open — the meaty end-gap.
center.title: The resurrection end-silence (Mark 16:8 · the unnarrated after)

cross_gospel.seam: comparative beats key on narrative beat + carried_by gospel; no verse or move handle joins a beat to the reader's selection. Method seam item (SS E requirement (a)/(b), SS I).
cross_gospel.seam_reader: the four gospels are lined up by episode, not verse by verse, so an episode cannot yet be matched to the verse you are reading.

beats.beat: female follower(s) travel to the tomb early on the first day
beats.note: MATT names two Marys; MARK three women with spices; LUKE a group with spices; JOHN Mary Magdalene alone

beats.beat: the sealing stone is found/made displaced from the tomb entrance
beats.note: MATT dramatizes an angel rolling it in real time; MARK/LUKE/JOHN find it already moved (divine passive)

beats.beat: the women/witness(es) enter or peer into the tomb
beats.note: MARK and LUKE enter bodily; JOHN has the disciples enter and Mary bend down to look; MATT omits an interior entry

beats.beat: the body of Jesus is discovered absent from its burial place
beats.note: framed as angelic declaration in MATT/MARK/LUKE and as empirical discovery-then-report in JOHN

beats.beat: one or more numinous figures (angel/young man/two men) are present at the tomb
beats.note: MATT one angel outside; MARK one young man inside; LUKE and JOHN two figures; JOHN's appear only in Mary's second visit

beats.beat: the numinous figure(s) are visually marked by whiteness/dazzling appearance
beats.note: lightning/snow (MATT), white robe (MARK), dazzling clothes (LUKE), white (JOHN)

beats.beat: the witnesses react with fear, dread, or bewilderment
beats.note: MATT guards struck down + women's mingled fear/joy; MARK alarm/terror; LUKE terror + bowing; JOHN grief rather than terror

beats.beat: the figure(s) address the witnesses with a speech-act interpreting the empty tomb
beats.note: MATT/MARK a commission; LUKE a rhetorical rebuke + reminder; JOHN only a 'why do you weep' question

beats.beat: the sought one is identified as the crucified Jesus
beats.note: MATT/MARK by the angelic naming, LUKE embedded in the passion-prediction; JOHN never verbalizes crucifixion in this scene

beats.beat: his absence from the tomb is explicitly declared ('he is not here')
beats.note: formulaic in the synoptics; JOHN dramatizes absence but never states the formula

beats.beat: his resurrected/raised status is announced (typically as divine passive)
beats.note: MATT/MARK/LUKE via the figures' proclamation; JOHN gestures at it only through the beloved disciple's belief and a scriptural aside

beats.beat: the witnesses are invited to view/verify the vacated burial spot
beats.note: MATT/MARK by directive ('come, see'); LUKE by finding no body; JOHN by inspection of the linen wrappings

beats.beat: a prior word of Jesus is invoked to frame what has happened
beats.note: MATT/MARK cite his earlier promise about Galilee; LUKE cites the passion-and-resurrection prediction; JOHN cites scripture instead

beats.beat: the witnesses depart from the tomb
beats.note: MATT hasten with fear+joy; MARK flee in terror; LUKE return to the eleven; JOHN Mary runs to Peter, disciples return home

beats.beat: the witnesses are commissioned/moved to report to the (male) disciples
beats.note: explicit commission in MATT/MARK; LUKE self-initiated report; JOHN Mary's spontaneous run to Peter/beloved disciple

beats.beat: the announcement is (or is to be) carried to Peter and the wider disciple circle
beats.note: MARK names Peter in the commission (and shorter ending); LUKE the eleven; JOHN Peter and the beloved disciple; MATT names 'his disciples' without Peter

beats.beat: a promise of future seeing/reunion with the risen Jesus is issued
beats.note: both locate it in Galilee via a 'he goes before you' formula; absent from LUKE and JOHN's tomb scene

beats.beat: male disciple(s) go to the tomb to verify the women's report
beats.note: LUKE Peter alone; JOHN Peter with the beloved disciple in a footrace

beats.beat: the linen burial cloths are seen lying in the tomb
beats.note: LUKE a single mention by Peter; JOHN elaborated as wrappings plus separately rolled head-cloth

beats.beat: a closing cognitive/affective state is left unresolved into full belief
beats.note: MARK women's fearful silence; LUKE Peter's amazement; contrast JOHN's beloved-disciple belief and MATT's commissioned joy
